commitResults.messageBody:
Move load and save failure rendering out of MyBff into Ui, preserving
the exact text and existing rollback behavior. MyBff now coordinates
operations without writing console responses directly, preparing for
a separate Storage extraction in the next increment.

Remove the leftover 100-task checks from additions and startup loading.
TaskList already uses a growing collection, and the existing UI plan
expects more than 100 tasks. Cover loading 101 tasks, adding a 102nd,
and preserving the full list across restart. Align the stale storage-test
expectation with the existing save error text.

Give the regular JAR the plain classifier so it no longer collides with
the runnable mybff.jar. This resolves Gradle's overlapping-output errors
when building the application distributions.

Trace intermittent growth-test failures to AccessDeniedException during
atomic replacement on Windows. Retry only access-denied replacement up
to five times, waiting 100 ms between attempts. Preserve atomic writes,
temporary-file cleanup, bounded failure handling, interruption status,
and in-memory rollback. Add real Windows file-lock checks for successful
recovery after a brief lock and unchanged data after a persistent lock.

Validation with Java 25.0.4:
- All eight exact-output UI cases pass, including growth beyond 100 tasks.
- Saving, restart, migration, malformed-file, rollback, and large-list
  persistence checks pass.
- Temporary and persistent Windows file-lock cases pass with exact
  console responses, saved-file assertions, and temporary-file cleanup.
- Gradle build succeeds; runnable-JAR deletion, restart, empty-list, and
  failed-save rollback checks pass.
- Refresh the test plans and retain the full console session records.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract task-file persistence from MyBff into Storage
commitResults.messageBody:
Move task loading, legacy-format decoding, atomic saving, temporary-file
cleanup, and bounded access-denied retries into a dedicated Storage
class. Accept a file path when constructing Storage so persistence is
independent of the console coordinator. Resolve the path once so a
filename without a directory also has a parent for temporary files.

Have load return a new TaskList only after all records are read
successfully, keeping partially loaded data out of MyBff. Delegate all
three save sites to Storage.save(tasks), leaving command routing,
user-facing error messages, and rollback decisions in MyBff.

Preserve data/mybff.txt, the v3 save format, legacy file support, task
ordering and completion flags, load-failure shutdown, and existing
save-failure behavior. Keep the current UI test expectations unchanged.

Validation with Java 25.0.4:
- All eight exact-output command-line UI cases pass.
- Saving, restart, format migration, malformed-file, large-list, and
  rollback checks pass.
- Temporary and persistent Windows file-lock checks pass.
- Runnable-JAR deletion and restart checks pass; Gradle build succeeds.

Use a separate UI session log after a transient log-file lock and allow
60 seconds for storage-test child processes after a host startup timeout.
Keep every test input, assertion, and application response unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract task-number parsing into Parser
commitResults.messageBody:
Add Parser.parseTaskIndex to interpret the argument of mark, unmark,
and delete commands and convert the displayed task number into a
zero-based index. Reuse it from both MyBff handlers instead of repeating
substring extraction, whitespace trimming, and integer conversion.

Remove the now-unnecessary commandWord parameter from the completion
handler. Keep list-bound validation in TaskList and error rendering in
Ui, preserving NumberFormatException handling and the existing invalid
task number response. Leave command routing, mutations, persistence,
and rollback unchanged.

Document the parser method's input and validation contract. This finishes
the remaining parsing extraction without adding command classes or
changing any command syntax or expected UI output.

Validation with Java 25.0.4:
- All eight exact-output UI cases pass, including invalid and overflowing
  task numbers, whitespace, deletion, status changes, and large lists.
- Storage, restart, migration, malformed-file, rollback, and Windows
  file-lock checks pass.
- Gradle build and runnable-JAR deletion/restart checks pass.
- Java style and diff whitespace checks pass.

Use the same test-run accommodations as the preceding iteration:
a separate UI log and 60-second storage child-process timeouts, with
all original commands and assertions preserved.

commitResults.messageTitle: Introduce Command and extract ListCommand
commitResults.messageBody:
Add an abstract Command with a shared execute(TaskList, Ui, Storage)
contract as the first step toward polymorphic command execution.
Extract the list action into ListCommand and have MyBff invoke it
through a Command reference.

Start with the read-only list action so this increment establishes the
command boundary without changing parsing, file writes, rollback, or
exit behavior. ListCommand delegates response formatting to Ui and
does not mutate the supplied tasks or storage. Keep command selection
in MyBff while the remaining actions are migrated in later increments.

Preserve exact list recognition, task order, status display, separators,
empty-list output, and rejection of list commands with extra arguments.
The common signature includes Storage for later mutating commands even
though ListCommand does not need to use it.

Validation with Java 25.0.4:
- All eight exact-output UI cases pass, covering empty and populated
  lists, invalid commands, status updates, deletion, and large lists.
- Saving, restart, migration, malformed-file, rollback, and Windows
  file-lock checks pass; the saving checks include a read-only list.
- Gradle build and runnable-JAR deletion/restart checks pass.
- Java style and diff whitespace checks pass.

Reuse the established test-run accommodations: a separate UI log and
60-second storage child-process timeouts, preserving all test inputs,
assertions, and expected responses.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract task addition and save rollback into AddCommand
commitResults.messageBody:
Add AddCommand as a Command subclass that stores a parsed Task. Move
appending, saving, save-failure rollback, and addition confirmation out
of MyBff into its execute method. Reuse the same command for todos,
deadlines, and events without coupling execution to input parsing.

Have MyBff parse the task and execute the new command through the
Command interface. Keep parse-error handling in the coordinator so
invalid input still produces the same response before any list change.

Preserve the existing order of operations: append, save, then confirm.
On IOException or SecurityException, remove the just-appended task,
report the standard save error, and omit the success message. Keep
command routing, task formatting, storage format, and separators intact.

Validation with Java 25.0.4:
- All eight exact-output UI cases pass, including all task types,
  rejected additions, whitespace, status updates, deletion, and large lists.
- Saving, restart, migration, malformed-file, and rollback checks pass.
- Temporary and persistent Windows file-lock cases pass, verifying that
  a failed addition does not change the original task list or file.
- Gradle build and runnable-JAR deletion/restart checks pass.
- Java style and diff whitespace checks pass.

Reuse the established separate UI log and 60-second storage process
timeouts while retaining every original test input and assertion.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract deletion and rollback into DeleteCommand
commitResults.messageBody:
Add a DeleteCommand subclass that holds a parsed zero-based task index.
Move list-index validation, removal, persistence, rollback, and success
reporting from MyBff into execute. Check the index at execution time so
the command operates on the list supplied through the Command contract.

Restore the same removed Task at its original index when saving throws
IOException or SecurityException. Preserve its type, completion status,
position, and the existing save error response; confirm deletion only
after the file has been saved successfully.

Keep task-number parsing in Parser and NumberFormatException handling
in MyBff's delegating handler. Preserve all command syntax,
invalid-number messages, separators, and task counts. This extends the
existing Command hierarchy without changing the remaining handlers.

Validation with Java 25.0.4:
- All eight exact-output UI cases pass, including deleting first, middle,
  and last tasks, invalid task numbers, and deletion from an empty list.
- Storage, restart, migration, malformed-file, rollback, and Windows
  file-lock checks pass.
- The runnable-JAR tests verify persistent deletion, an empty saved
  list, and restoration of the original order when saving fails.
- Gradle build, Java style checks, and diff whitespace checks pass.

Reuse the established separate UI log and 60-second storage process
timeouts without changing any test input, assertion, or expected output.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract completion changes into CompletionCommand
commitResults.messageBody:
Move task-index validation, mark/unmark updates, saving, and rollback
from MyBff into a Command subclass. Capture the parsed index and desired
completion state, validating against the task list at execution time.

Share one command for the two status changes because their validation
and persistence behavior are identical. Restore the exact prior status
on IOException or SecurityException and show success only after saving.
Keep task-number parsing and malformed-number reporting in MyBff for
this incremental refactoring; preserve all existing console responses.

Validation with Java 25.0.4:
- All eight exact-output UI cases pass.
- Storage, restart, migration, error and rollback checks pass.
- Temporary and persistent Windows file-lock checks pass.
- Runnable-JAR regression checks and the Gradle build pass.
- Modified Java files pass style and diff whitespace checks.

Reuse the established separate UI log and 60-second storage process

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract farewell and exit signaling into ExitCommand
commitResults.messageBody:
Add a default isExit method to Command that returns false and override
it in ExitCommand to return true. Let ExitCommand display the existing
farewell through Ui without changing the task list or saving the file.

Move recognition of the exact bye command into MyBff's command router.
Have the router execute ExitCommand through the Command contract and
return its exit signal to the main loop. Preserve the farewell's closing
line by stopping before the normal response ending is printed.

Keep command construction in MyBff for this standalone increment; the
next step can move it into Parser. Preserve EOF handling, input trimming,
rejection of bye with extra text, and all existing command responses.

Validation with Java 25.0.4:
- All eight exact-output UI cases pass, including farewell formatting
  and rejection of bye with extra text.
- Storage, restart, migration, error and rollback checks pass.
- Temporary and persistent Windows file-lock checks pass.
- Runnable-JAR regression checks and the Gradle build pass.
- Modified Java files pass style and diff whitespace checks.

Reuse the established separate UI log and 60-second storage process
timeouts without changing test inputs, assertions, or expected output.

commitResults.messageTitle: Complete command parsing and simplify MyBff's execution loop
commitResults.messageBody:
Add Parser.parse to construct ListCommand, AddCommand, DeleteCommand,
CompletionCommand, or ExitCommand from user input. Keep parsing free of
task mutations and user interaction, and hide command constants and
parsing helpers now that callers only need the command factory.

Replace MyBff's command router and three operation-specific handlers
with one parse, execute, and isExit flow. Retain separate handling for
malformed task numbers and MyBffException to preserve the exact existing
error messages. Keep index validation and save rollback in commands.

Preserve exact list/bye matching, task syntax, EOF handling, startup
load-error behavior, farewell formatting, and console cleanup. This
completes the requested Command hierarchy stretch goal while keeping
the application's MyBff identity and existing behavior.

Validation with Java 25.0.4:
- All eight exact-output UI cases pass.
- Storage, restart, migration, malformed-file and rollback checks pass.
- Temporary and persistent Windows file-lock checks pass.
- Runnable-JAR regression checks and the Gradle build pass.
- Modified Java files pass style and diff whitespace checks.

Reuse the established separate UI log and 60-second storage process
timeouts without changing test inputs, assertions, or expected output.
